source-integrity.freshness: FY27 Q2 primary filing/release dated 2026-09-09 plus 2026-09-25 independent valuation
source-integrity.duplicateOriginCollapse: issuer release/8-K treated as one primary origin for repeated financial claims
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: primary issuer/SEC operating evidence separated from independent S&P-derived market data

company-underwriting.operatingFinancialTrajectory: FY27 Q2 ARR $1.231B +25%, SaaS ARR $847M +36%, revenue $309M +17%, operating cash flow $45M and FCF $37M; GAAP operating loss widened to $59M while adjusted operating margin was about 20%.
company-underwriting.contractsBacklogCustomersSuppliers: RPO reached about $1.9B and current RPO $931M; SaaS customer and spend expansion support demand visibility. Identity-security delivery is software-centric with limited physical supply-chain exposure.
company-underwriting.balanceSheetRunwayDebtDilution: Positive operating and free cash flow reduce near-term funding risk, but share count has risen materially since the IPO and GAAP profitability remains negative.
company-underwriting.governanceCapitalAllocation: Founder-led execution and raised ARR outlook are constructive; recent public-company history is short and GAAP/non-GAAP divergence lowers confidence.
company-underwriting.pricingPowerConcentration: 113% NRR, high-90s gross retention and rising ARR per SaaS customer support pricing/value capture, while suite competition remains material.
catalysts: Agentic Suites and non-human identity adoption
AI-driven ARR above $70M and growing pipeline
company-underwriting.thesis: Identity governance is becoming a control-plane requirement as human and machine identities proliferate; SailPoint shows strong recurring growth and AI monetization, but valuation and GAAP losses constrain asymmetry.
company-underwriting.keyRisk: High expectations and valuation compress sharply if SaaS/AI ARR growth slows or broader security suites erode standalone differentiation.
company-underwriting.nextCatalyst: FY27 Q3 execution and Agentic Suite adoption.

thesisQuality.basis: 25% ARR and 36% SaaS ARR growth, high retention and expanding AI-driven ARR demonstrate strong product-market fit in identity security.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: ARR/revenue growth, positive $37M quarterly FCF and ~20% adjusted margin are strong, offset by a $59M GAAP operating loss.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At Sep-25 the stock traded near $20.64, about $11.8B market cap, ~10.1x sales, ~57.5x forward earnings and ~66x FCF, demanding relative to current profitability.

catalystScore.basis: AI-driven ARR above $70M, >30% of net new ARR from AI solutions and raised FY27 ARR outlook provide several source-supported near/medium catalysts.

governancePower.basis: Founder-led execution and guidance delivery are constructive, but short post-IPO history and GAAP/non-GAAP divergence limit the band.

alignment2036.basis: Identity control for humans, machines and autonomous agents is foundational to secure AI/cloud adoption across plausible 2036 enterprise futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Unified identity platform expands across human, machine, data and agentic use cases, though revenue remains concentrated in one broad security category.

bottleneckControl.basis: Enterprise identity authorization is a meaningful security control point with integration and governance switching friction, but credible suite substitutes exist.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Identity governance demand persists across cloud, hybrid and agentic architectures, though security-budget and platform-bundling scenarios remain risks.

substitutionResilience.basis: Deep integrations, retention and platform breadth support switching friction, offset by Microsoft/cloud/security-suite substitution risk.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Software/SaaS delivery has limited physical supply-chain dependency; resilience is instead bounded by cloud/infrastructure partners and service availability.

pricingPower.basis: 113% NRR, high-90s gross retention and rising ARR per SaaS customer support meaningful expansion economics without proving exceptional structural pricing power.

riskEvidence.basis: Strong recurring growth is offset by demanding valuation, GAAP losses, dilution and competitive bundling risk.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current primary filing/release covers operating metrics and cash flow and independent current market data covers valuation; confidence is reduced by limited public-company history and incomplete competitor economics.

scoreRecord.thesis: SailPoint is a strong identity-security compounder with accelerating agentic demand, but current valuation leaves limited room for execution misses.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Growth deceleration or suite substitution compresses premium valuation.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: FY27 Q3 and Agentic Suite adoption.
